cards.title: Published scattering-length parameterization

source_refs.value: Cikojevic et al., Phys. Rev. A 102, 033335 (2020), Table I

open_questions: The original coupled-channel potential/model is not fully printed in the target paper.

checks.reason: The three parameter rows are printed in the cited primary-source table and the target paper identifies the same coupled-channel model.
The interpolant returns all nine published table values to floating-point precision.
The reconstructed delta-a zero lies near the independently printed B_c=56.85 G.

cards.title: Effective attraction and locked density ratio

checks.reason: Both relations are explicitly printed in the main text.
The generated ratio remains positive and delta-a changes sign only once in the plotted interval.

cards.title: Coupled Gross-Pitaevskii and LHY functional
open_questions: The per-curve atom numbers and therefore the author's exact initial arrays for Main Fig. 4 are not published; the stated preparation procedure is independently implementable.

checks.reason: The coupled GPE, GP energy, LHY energy, and its functional derivative are printed consecutively in the supplement.
Differentiating the printed simplified LHY energy reproduces the printed chemical-potential term.

cards.title: Equilibrium densities and physical length scale

source_refs.value: Petrov, Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 155302 (2015), Eqs. for n_i^(0) and xi

checks.reason: The equilibrium-density expression is printed in Petrov and the length rescaling is printed in the same derivation cited by the target paper.
The density ratio from n_i^(0) equals sqrt(a22/a11).
n_i^(0) has inverse-volume units and xi has length units.

source_refs.value: Petrov, Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 155302 (2015), dimensionless GP equation

At mu=-0.061 the radial BVP returns N_tilde=18.649, matching the printed 18.65 fold.

cards.title: Critical numbers and observable size

source_refs.value: Petrov stability discussion: N_tilde,c=18.65 and zero-energy threshold 22.55

open_questions: The paper does not state how the radial theory density was mapped to the plotted experimental 1/e^2 Gaussian width.

checks.reason: Petrov explicitly prints the 18.65 instability and 22.55 zero-energy thresholds used by the target-paper curves.
The 22.55 profile has zero energy within the solver tolerance and is narrower than the 18.65 metastability fold.

source_refs.value: Supplement Eqs. (1)--(2) and Fig. S1 text

checks.reason: The modulation trajectory, Gaussian period average, and all numerical parameters are printed in the supplement.
The generated central optical gradient cancels gravity to better than 1e-4 relative error.
Using the source panel's signed force-gradient convention, the curvature is positive at -15 micrometres, negative at +15 micrometres, and has magnitude about 20 Hz.

cards.title: Thomas-Fermi expansion scaling

source_refs.value: Supplement Fig. S2: GPE free and 12 Hz confined evolution

open_questions: The atom number of the Supplement Fig. S2 calibration condensate is not printed.

checks.reason: The supplement states that the two curves are GPE evolutions in free space and with 12 Hz vertical confinement, and prints the initial trap/scattering parameters elsewhere.
b_i(0)=1 and db_i/dt(0)=0.
The free curve expands faster than the 12 Hz confined curve after release.

open_questions: The per-curve initial atom numbers for Main Fig. 4 are not printed.
The atom number of the Supplement Fig. S2 calibration condensate is not printed.
The paper does not state the density-to-Gaussian fitting algorithm used for its simulated Main Fig. 4 widths.

checks.reason: The supplement explicitly specifies the initial state preparation, coupled local-LHY equations, split-step technique, no-loss Fig. 4 evolution, and free/12 Hz S2 comparison.
The LHY chemical potentials agree with finite differences of the independently implemented LHY energy density on the smoke path.
The paper-scale contract requires 512^3 production, 640^3 spatial refinement, and a halved time step, with scenario-specific boxes that contain the 25 ms droplet and 12 ms expansion trajectories.
Acceptance rejects trajectories whose outer 10% FFT-box shell contains 1e-4 or more of the norm.
